Commentary.Commentary: We are back after the innings break and it is Ireland to chase 141 runs in 20 overs. The Umpires and the players are making their way to the center to start the second innings. Andy Balbirnie and Paul Stirling will open up for Ireland. Richard Ngarava comes to bowl. Lets go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the game looks slightly in favor of Ireland as of now. Zimbabwe will be hoping for their bowlers to defend the total and pick some early wickets. Ireland, on the other hand, will be hoping for a gritty start from their openers. Which side will come out on top in this decider game? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

Ireland will be slightly upset with their effort in the middle overs, as they were off to a flier. They failed to break the Ryan Burl-Clive Madande partnership. Had they done that, the total would have been much lower. Joshua Little, Craig Young, and Gareth Delany chipped in with two wickets. The rest of their bowlers were wicketless.

So, Zimbabwe ended their inning at 140/6, thanks to the fifth-wicket partnership from Ryan Burl and Clive Madande. They will certainly be happy with their effort, as they were off to a tame start. They were 61 for 4 inside 10 overs, but the fifth-wicket partnership of Clive Madande and Ryan Burl helped them. Clive Madande fell in the 17th over, and Ryan Burl soon followed suit. Ryan Burl scored 36 while Clive Madande was dismissed on 27.
A single to end the innings! Full and outside off, Luke Jongwe drives it to covers for one. Zimbabwe end their innings for 140/6.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle, followed by the two Zimbabwe openers, Wesley Madhevere and Tinashe Kamunhukamwe. Mark Adair has the new ball in hand and will begin the proceedings. Let's go...
PITCH REPORT - The pitch here is a new and fresh one. There are a few cracks and some grassy areas in the middle. The pacers will look to attack the area where there is some grass.
Ryan Burl, the skipper of Zimbabwe, says that they were going to bat first, so that's good. Adds that they will look to put a good score on the board. Ends by mentioning the changes on their side.

Paul Stirling, the skipper of Ireland, says that they will bowl first. It adds that they did well last time when they bowled first, so they will do the same. He says that they will look to chase, as they are better at that, and will look to put pressure on Zimbabwe early on. Ends by saying that they will go with their original side.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Andy Balbirnie, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Mark Adair, Gareth Delany, Barry McCarthy (In for Theo van Woerkom), Craig Young, Joshua Little.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Wesley Madhevere, Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, Brian Bennett, Tony Munyonga (In for Sean Williams), Ryan Burl (C), Clive Madande (WK), Brandon Mavuta (In for Trevor Gwandu), Luke Jongwe, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani, Wellington Masakadza (In for Tadiwanashe Marumani).
TOSS - Ireland have won the toss and will BOWL first.

Both the games were a last-over thriller, and with the kind of cricket we've seen, an intense final is anticipated. However, Zimbabwe will face a tough challenge without Sikandar Raza. So, who will win? We shall find out together. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! Zimbabwe and Ireland are set to face off in the decider match of their three-game T20I series at the Harare Sports Club. The series has been full of excitement, with Zimbabwe narrowly winning the first match with just one wicket on the final ball and Ireland coming back strong to win the second one with four wickets.
... MATCH DAY ...

Time to fasten your seatbelts as we enter the decider game of the Ireland tour of Zimbabwe. We have had two last-over thrillers, with the series leveled 1-1 so far. In the first match, the hosts chose to field first. Andrew Balbirnie, Lorcan Tucker, Harry Tector, and Gareth Delany contributed to a total of 147 runs for 8 wickets. Sikandar Raza took three wickets for 28 runs. In the chase, Zimbabwe struggled, but Sikandar Raza's 65 off 42 balls and Clive Mandande's 20 off 11 balls at the very end helped them win by one wicket on the last ball. But Sikandar Raza was involved in an altercation with two Ireland players during the 14th over of Zimbabwe's chase. Raza received two demerit points for the offense, which took his total to four in the last 24 months, leading to a two-match ban. He was out for the second game and will be out in this one as well. In the second game, the visitors chose to field first. They had a target of 165 runs and were off to a shaky start, but Curtis Campher and Tector in the middle steadied the ship, with George Dockrell finishing things off in style with just two balls left. Thus, given the quality of cricket we have witnessed thus far, an exciting final is anticipated at the Harare Sports Club. But it will be a difficult task for Zimbabwe to defeat the Irish without Sikandar Raza. So, can the hosts bounce back now and win the series? Or will the visitors come up with yet another special performance? We shall find out, as this game promises to be a cracker.
